source: Live read-only Supabase SQL catalog; full pg_aggregate row_to_json plus pg_proc canonical identity and privilege metadata.
source_limitation: pg_get_functiondef(oid) rejects aggregate entries (SQLSTATE 42809). Aggregate definitions were instead recovered from every exposed pg_aggregate catalog attribute, rather than invented CREATE AGGREGATE SQL or native compiled source.
source_md5_definition: MD5 PostgreSQL concat_ws('|', oid, pg_get_function_identity_arguments, pg_get_function_arguments, pg_get_function_result, row_to_json(pg_aggregate)::text)

findings.evidence: 157 PostgreSQL catalog aggregates use valid transition/state/operator references, no SECURITY DEFINER; absence of selected helpers is allowed by aggregate kind.
All have SQL-level EXECUTE grants to anon and authenticated. Direct role catalog grants alone do not prove HTTP route exposure, RLS bypass or runtime function access.

next: pg_catalog window routines 1/15, then SQL language routines 1/50, then remaining provider hosted surfaces
